PullRequest.Title: Workspace settings: stop verifying async tokenization in this repo
PullRequest.Body:

This repository's `.vscode/settings.json` turns on `editor.experimental.asyncTokenizationVerification` (added in #179864). Its schema describes it as "Controls whether async tokenization should be verified against legacy background tokenization. Might slow down tokenization. For debugging only." This PR removes that line.

**What the setting does.** For every TextMate-tokenized file open in an editor in this workspace, the window's main thread runs the legacy background tokenizer over the whole file in idle time (`DefaultBackgroundTokenizer`, until every line is valid), and the syntax colors come from it. The worker tokenizes the file as well, only to compare. The first time a line differs in a window, it shows an error notification and sends the `asyncTokenizationMismatchingTokens` telemetry event.

**The trade-off, for the setting's owner (hediet) to decide:** without the line, this workspace no longer runs that check, so it no longer shows the notification or sends that event. Contributors who still want it can turn the setting on in their user settings. `editor.experimental.asyncTokenization: true` stays: it matches the default, but keeping it means a user-level `false` doesn't turn the worker off in this repo. #179864 turned the setting on "to investigate a reported bug". Samples of `editor.tokenizedLine` from this workspace will also report `tokenizationSetting` 1 (async) instead of 2 (verification).

Users are not affected: the setting is off by default.

## Measured on my machine

Code OSS dev build, a clone of this repository: opening a 47,000-line file, scrolling, typing and finding. The numbers are the window's main-thread CPU time added up over the whole scenario, not a single freeze.

| | With the setting | Without |
|---|---|---|
| Main-thread background tokenization (`_backgroundTokenizeForAtLeast1ms`) | 3,837 ms | 0 ms |
| TextMate regex matching in the window (`vscode-oniguruma`) | 2,875 ms | 96 ms |

## How to test

Reload the window after pulling: the setting is only read when a file's tokenization starts. Open a large file in this repository, for example `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts`. Syntax colors look the same as before; they now come from the worker. To see the change, record a profile in the Performance tab of **Developer: Toggle Developer Tools** while opening and scrolling the file: with the setting, `_backgroundTokenizeForAtLeast1ms` runs on the main thread; without it, it doesn't.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The workspace enabled debug verification for ordinary contributor editing. Every attached, eligible TextMate model was background-tokenized both by the shared worker and by a legacy tokenizer in main-thread idle slices, with separate debug token/state stores and per-line equality checks. CPU work scales with file contents and subsequent invalidation, even after grammars and the worker are warm.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Strong static evidence of avoidable main-thread regex tokenization and duplicate token/state retention when opening large repository files or editing text that invalidates many following lines, competing with UI responsiveness. No independent timing measurements were performed.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Remove the repository's verification=true override, allowing the default false (unless explicitly enabled in user settings). With async tokenization still enabled, worker-capable attached models use the existing shared worker as their background tokenizer rather than performing an additional full-file legacy background pass on the UI thread and retaining verification stores.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The deleted workspace setting forces verification true; editorConfigurationSchema.ts:111-115 defaults it to false. TextMateTokenizationFeature._createTokenizationSupport (textMateTokenizationFeatureImpl.ts:312-317) supplies that configuration through TextMateTokenizationSupport.backgroundTokenizerShouldOnlyVerifyTokens. TokenizerSyntaxTokenBackend.todo_resetTokenization:148-176 then skips the authoritative worker path, starts DefaultBackgroundTokenizer, and separately starts the worker for verification. DefaultBackgroundTokenizer (textModelTokens.ts:463-552) repeatedly tokenizes invalid lines on the window thread until all states are valid; content changes restart this work. Disabling verification instead uses the existing worker as the authoritative tokenizer and does not instantiate the default background tokenizer when worker tokenization is supported. getLineTokens:286-296 also stops maintaining/comparing the duplicate verification token store. Blame identifies the introducing commit for the removed base line.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the repository workspace and attach one or more TextMate-tokenized files with the default user configuration.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening/editing does not wait for whole-file background tokenization; visible-range synchronous tokenization remains. On cold start, authoritative worker background results now depend on worker initialization, WASM and grammar loading, and delivery of token/state batches. Previously the same worker started for verification while a main-thread legacy tokenizer supplied authoritative background results. The diff removes that duplicate full-file UI-thread pass; it does not add worker initialization or require all background tokens before interaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize the shared web worker and send model URI, all lines, version, language and tokenization settings through the worker proxy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced worker initialization per factory lifetime; one full-content model message and initial length-setting message per attached model/controller, not per line.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same shared worker initialization and model serialization occurred for verification. The setting removal changes which background token store consumes its results, not this boundary-call count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initialization gates worker background results, now authoritative, but does not gate initial text interaction or require full-file completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read extension grammar resources through IFileService; the worker requests grammar reads through its host channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Driven by required grammar scopes and dependencies, shared across models through grammar caches; not one filesystem read per source line or source file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both main-thread and worker grammars were already needed and loaded for verification. Their resource-loading mechanisms and caching are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Grammar availability gates tokenization for the affected language; worker grammar availability now gates authoritative worker background results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the Oniguruma WASM resource in each execution context and, where applicable, load remote/browser extension grammar resources using fetch or IRequestService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: WASM loading is cached per main-thread service/shared worker lifetime. Remote grammar requests follow grammar dependencies and language cache misses, not model-line cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same main-thread and worker resources were loaded with verification enabled; no new fetch loop or remote boundary is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold WASM/grammar fetches gate the corresponding tokenizer. The worker's cold readiness becomes relevant to authoritative background results; visible-range main-thread tokenization remains available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize token chunks and state deltas, send them to the window, deserialize/rebase them, and install background results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Chunks contain up to 201 processed lines, potentially fewer at the time-yield threshold; total serialized data scales with tokenized contents, not one message per line by design.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The worker serialized and sent the same chunks to a separate debug store while the legacy main-thread tokenizer supplied authoritative results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delivery now updates authoritative tokens and states rather than the debug verification store. This is a changed consumer/placement on the background-coloring path, not an increase in serialization frequency. Initial rendering can still use synchronous visible-range tokens.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of attached eligible models, their total lines/bytes, and distinct grammar languages/dependencies. A single shared worker serves the window, not one worker per file.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One shared worker event loop serializes regex execution across model controllers. Each attached model has a controller; detached controllers are disposed. Cold main-thread module/WASM loading uses Promise.all as before. Worker tokenization sends chunks of up to 201 lines and yields after approximately 20 ms of work. The old additional main-thread tokenizer used coalesced idle callbacks and roughly 1–2 ms slices.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Worker creation is coalesced by _workerProxyPromise. Worker grammar creation caches promises by encoded language ID, including pending/rejected promises; the diff does not alter failure retries or negative caching. Main-thread grammar factory and Oniguruma loading also remain cached. Warm files of the same language reuse the worker and grammar; each attachment still sends the model contents as before. Disabling verification removes the duplicate debug token/state stores.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: configuration default, callback wiring, authoritative/debug branch selection, worker sharing, batching, resource loading and disposal were traced in source.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings were independently measured. The practical balance of cold-worker startup versus removed UI-thread regex work depends on file size, grammar complexity and resource-cache warmth.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This removes duplicate main-thread tokenization and verification retention while preserving an existing worker pipeline. Recorded the concrete performance fix and base-line blame provenance separately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll, type, or make edits that invalidate many following lines in an already attached repository file.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Input and visible-range tokenization remain synchronous on the window thread. Content changes are sent to the existing worker without awaiting completion; worker updates eventually replace background tokens. Edits formerly also restarted the legacy idle tokenizer, and token reads compared authoritative and debug stores. Those duplicate activities disappear by default.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send each model-change event to the worker and request retokenization of heuristic-token ranges when needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One change message per content event, regardless of lines represented by the event. Explicit range requests follow changed heuristic ranges; they do not occur unconditionally per model line.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Content events were already sent to the verification worker. Heuristic range request routing existed before the change; the worker becomes authoritative rather than debug-only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Sending is asynchronous; updated worker results are not awaited before typing proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and return incrementally recomputed token/state chunks; rebase results over pending edits in the window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Scales with invalidated tokenized lines and pending edits, with chunks of at most 201 lines and earlier time-based yields; not one result message for every individual line.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same result stream was deserialized and rebased for debug stores, while an additional main-thread tokenizer computed authoritative tokens. The diff changes the consumer, not the underlying serialization algorithm or per-chunk work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authoritative background updates now consume the same worker result stream. Visible-range tokenization remains available while results are pending.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Content-change event count, payload bytes, invalidated lines until tokenizer state converges, visible ranges and outstanding edits. A small edit need not retokenize the whole file; state-changing edits can invalidate a long suffix.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One worker executes model jobs; tokenization yields after approximately 20 ms and sends bounded line chunks. Model change notifications remain asynchronous. The removed main-thread idle loop was separate duplicate execution, not a concurrency limit on the worker.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The shared worker, language grammar and valid line states remain warm. Incremental state invalidation is preserved. The worker's per-model RunOnceScheduler coalesces tokenization after changes with a 10 ms delay; content-change messages themselves remain uncoalesced as before. No new cache or key retention is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: content listeners, idle-tokenizer restart, visible-range tokenization, debouncer, result batching and verification comparisons were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual savings and any cold/lagging-worker visible-token fallback cost depend on grammar, edit locality and scrolling rate; source establishes removed duplicate work without asserting measured latency gains.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence regression: worker edit propagation and result processing already ran. The diff removes legacy duplicate work and per-token-read verification by default.

Scenarios.Scenario: Models ineligible for worker syncing, models too large for tokenization, or contributors explicitly retaining verification in user settings.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For models too large for worker syncing but otherwise tokenizable, the factory still returns undefined and the backend uses the legacy tokenizer. Models too large for tokenization skip tokenizer initialization. A user-level verification=true still selects the prior debug-verification branch because the workspace no longer overrides it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For worker-eligible opt-in models, create/dispose controller mirrors and propagate edits/results; skip worker syncing when isTooLargeForSyncing is true.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One controller lifetime per attachment; no controller/model messages for size-rejected models. Explicit verification retains the same chunking and event counts described in the other scenarios.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same eligibility guards, controller cleanup and fallback existed before the diff; explicit verification retains the prior behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fallback does not wait for worker results. Explicit verification continues to use legacy authoritative background tokenization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Eligible attached models and their invalid lines; configured size thresholds bound whether tokenization/syncing occurs. No new per-line boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fallback uses coalesced main-thread idle callbacks; explicit verification runs that idle tokenizer alongside the same shared worker. These are unchanged configurations after resolving settings.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing grammar/module caches are unchanged. Explicit user opt-in preserves duplicate verification stores; unsupported worker models retain existing fallback behavior. Detachment still disposes controllers and removes worker models.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: size guards, configuration lookup, tokenizer selection and attachment cleanup were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence of oversized models and user-level opt-ins is unknown but does not change the traced unchanged execution branches.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression for these branches; the removed repository override does not remove fallback or prohibit explicit verification.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the sole changed file and complete diff against base 0cd87f75609c475a29750f73668e0db2d84418c3. No introduced high-confidence performance issues found. Traced defaults, tokenization consumers, cold/warm resource loading, worker serialization/batching, edits, size fallbacks and cleanup. Recorded the removal of duplicate main-thread verification tokenization as a regression fix with introducing commit ee88620afc77cd8f92a98a95574a88cd74b4b9c7 from base-line blame. Static review only.
